approval_required_for: Choosing a wrapper_top_module, compute cell, AXI width, simulator executable, or board target when current exact Vivado evidence does not uniquely identify it; request bounded approval instead of guessing.
Any architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, numeric-policy, tolerance, or major template change.

Changing the immutable checkpoint, stimulus, independent target-model reference, generated semantic testbench contract, exact sample-project wrapper or simulation source hashes, or Transformer-block weight boundary.
Any lower-layer reopening without a current hash-bound trace that directly contradicts a named certified invariant; a SACG-approved contract change that invalidates the invariant is also required.
Any promotion to Vivado synthesis, implementation, bitstream generation, runtime-ABI release, or board runtime before all three debug layers and all current board gates pass.

current real Vivado export facts and selected-cell evidence, if available
active SACG contamination barriers and retry requests

structured board-interface selector interpretation with cited source paths and Vivado cell facts
resolved wrapper_top_module and AXI interface facts only when directly evidenced

Do not infer or manually fill wrapper_top_module, compute_slot_abi.selected_cell_id, AXI width, or paths. If the cited evidence leaves multiple candidates, stop for bounded approval rather than guessing.

simulation identity-binding evidence and command authorization evidence

consumes: prior repair execution feedback and raw VCS runner evidence
current board simulation manifest and exact source identity

source index for generated board sources
current exact source identity and simulation manifest

exact wrapper and simulation source hashes

executable_actions.rationale: The existing multilayer-pipeline report is not executable evidence because the real tool was dependency-skipped. Do not run or promote later gates until these prerequisites pass.

consumes: immutable checkpoint, stimulus, target-model output, numeric policy, and exact wrapper/source hashes
executable_actions.on_failure: If termination is external or schema-invalid, execute the named capability repairs and rerun without source edits. executable_actions.rationale: Once board discovery, AXI/DDR identity, and multilayer prerequisites pass, execute the real VCS board simulation with the unchanged target checkpoint, deterministic stimulus, independent target-model expected output, frozen comparison policy, generated semantic testbench, exact wrapper, and complete bound Transformer-block weights. Capture current termination provenance and analyze the earliest valid boundary; no board pass is inferred from compilation.

live lower-layer certificates and elastic pipeline timing invariant
executable_actions.on_failure: Remain needs_repair with no RTL patch and no lower-layer reopening. If the trace does not directly contradict a certified invariant, retain leaf and connected-kernel certificates and repair only the unresolved board verification or wrapper integration contract.

failure localization and causal repair context

executable_actions.rationale: If the fresh VCS run fails, the hierarchical policy requires current board boundary tracing and targeted replay before any code repair. A lower-layer revalidation is permitted only if the current hash-bound trace directly contradicts a named certified lower-layer invariant.

observations: The earliest current deterministic failure is real_tool.case_board_interface_discovery: the selector failed to emit a valid structured interpretation, wrapper_top_module is missing, the selected compute slot is not a Vivado cell fact, and the required AXI width is unresolved. This is a board-interface discovery and verification-capability failure, not evidence of an RTL root cause.

functional_sim and all dependent board gates are not executable in the current DAG. Existing produced reports marked pass or fail do not replace a current real-tool execution when the gate status is not_run or dependency-skipped. No board-level value, numeric, order, AXI, DDR, liveness, output-frontier, or board-scope weight-consumption claim exists.

The operator-leaf and single-transformer-layer certificates are live hash-validated lower-layer evidence. No current hash-bound boundary trace contradicts a named lower-layer invariant, so neither lower layer may be reopened. The connected kernel's certified semantics are elastic and variable-latency: preserve boundary order and required cross-token overlap; do not require strict same-cycle start or finish across unequal-latency stages.

The prior board replay reported 1792 ingress beats and zero accepted core-egress beats after an external_or_unattributed runner-owned exit 86. That frontier symptom is localization evidence only; it is not a kernel root cause and cannot reopen the connected kernel. The prior diagnosis is historical when its live source hash or gate binding is invalid.

Prior repair feedback also reports invalid or missing schema fields in dynamic records 4 and 5 and an unresolved SPATIALACC_PIPELINE_TRACE emitter. The supplied testbench must not be patched speculatively; emitter ownership and source hash must be established before any event-schema repair.

sacg_memory_truth reports six open retry requests and fifteen active current-scope contamination barriers. Rejected Stage7 and Stage8 artifacts are usable only as debug evidence. The refined retry contract may supersede same-stage retry blockers only after all current-stage checks pass; it does not authorize promotion now.

Any future functional pass must bind a complete Transformer-block checkpoint tensor catalog, deterministic or real input provenance, independent target-model inference on the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus, resolved frozen numeric policy, generated semantic testbench hashes, and executed evidence that every required bound weight was consumed. On-disk weight files or manifests alone are insufficient.

Cross-layer consistency remains unproven at board scope across model and shape metadata, data order, numeric policy, memory addressing and DDR image layout, runtime lifecycle, AXI protocol, implementation facts, and board wrapper identity. The missing board semantic-evidence report is a downstream evidence gap, not permission to infer correctness.
proposed_actions: Repair the progressive/final board-interface selector contract using only current exact sample-project materials and cited Vivado facts; rerun case_board_interface_discovery before any dependent gate.
Rebind the current board simulation identity and canonical VCS compile plan to the discovered exact wrapper/source hashes, exact Vivado export contexts, and authorized simulator executable.
Implement the planned distinct VCS termination-provenance capability and conditional dynamic-event-emitter ownership attribution before relying on another semantic replay.
Rerun the current board layer in dependency order with the immutable checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, numeric policy, semantic testbench, Transformer-block weight catalog, and bound loader.

If a fresh real simulation produces a deterministic failure, collect a current board boundary trace and targeted replay first, then repair only the localized current-layer integration slice. Reopen a lower layer only if that trace directly contradicts a named certified invariant.
Do not promote to synthesis, implementation, bitstream, runtime ABI, or board runtime until every required current-layer gate and board semantic-evidence checker passes.
risks: Guessing wrapper_top_module, compute cell, AXI width, simulator executable, or source paths could bind the run to a non-user-supplied design and contaminate all downstream evidence.
Treating a dependency-skipped simulation or a stale diagnosis as executed evidence could incorrectly establish liveness, numeric correctness, output order, weight consumption, or a causal RTL defect.
Repairing RTL or reopening the certified connected kernel from the ingress-to-egress frontier symptom would violate the hierarchical repair loop without a current direct core-boundary contradiction.

Changing checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, tolerance, numeric comparison policy, generated testbench contract, weights, manifests, or exact wrapper/source hashes would invalidate the repair comparison.
Failure to distinguish AXI/prefetch progress from output or lifecycle-frontier progress can mislocalize a board integration failure.
A missing verifier capability must be repaired as a checker or golden-reference capability, not reported as hardware correctness.
Failure to restrict board semantic evidence and weight coverage to Transformer blocks could incorrectly impose tail-model requirements or alter the DUT golden boundary.
